paragraphs: Friend, this passage opens with the LORD sending Jeremiah on a search. "If you can find a single person, anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth, then I will forgive the city." (Jeremiah 5:1) The LORD is hunting for a reason to forgive, and He hasn't stopped hunting. That's the heart of Him, and it's the first thing I want you to carry out of here.

Now look at what He finds. The people say "As surely as the LORD lives," but they are swearing falsely (Jeremiah 5:2). The LORD struck them and they felt no pain, and they refused to repent (Jeremiah 5:3), then they said "He will not do anything" (Jeremiah 5:12). Friend, ignoring God's warning is no joke, so say His name and mean it, and listen when He answers.

And here's the good news: even with the hard things coming, the LORD says, "Yet even in those days… I will not make a full end of you." (Jeremiah 5:18) Warning and mercy are in the same breath. I know that kind of mercy, because He reached into a dark drawer for me. So baker, don't just say His name. Take His Word seriously, let it shape what you do, and trust that He's still looking for those who turn back to Him.
